config.title: scroll-snap

intro.title: scroll-snap
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple image gallery with smooth, controlled scrolling using CSS scroll-snap. You'll learn how to create containers that snap to specific positions when scrolling stops, making navigation more precise and user-friendly. The main technologies involved are CSS properties like scroll-snap-type, scroll-snap-align, and scroll-padding. By the end, you'll understand how to implement scroll snapping to enhance scrolling experiences on websites and applications.
intro.usecase: Scroll-snap is essential for creating polished, controlled scrolling experiences in modern web interfaces. You'll see this pattern in product galleries where images snap into place for clean viewing, onboarding tutorials that guide users through steps, and mobile carousels that ensure content aligns perfectly. As a developer, implementing scroll-snap improves usability in dashboards with side-scrolling data panels, horizontal navigation menus, and interactive storytelling components. This CSS feature transforms janky scrolling into smooth, intentional transitions that enhance user engagement.

objectives: Implement scroll-snap properties on a container element to enable snapping behavior
Configure scroll-snap-type to control the strictness and direction of snapping
Apply scroll-snap-align to child elements to define their snap positions
Construct a horizontal image carousel using scroll-snap techniques
Manipulate scroll-snap-stop to control whether scrolling can skip snap points
Integrate scroll-margin and scroll-padding to adjust snap alignment offsets
Initialize a vertical document layout with mandatory section snapping

steps.title: Set up the HTML container structure
steps.instruction: Create a parent container with class 'scroll-container' and three child containers with classes 'item-1', 'item-2', and 'item-3' in your HTML file.
steps.hint: You'll need to create a div with class 'scroll-container' and nest three divs inside it, each with their respective class names.

steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a parent container with three child elements ready for scroll-snap styling.
successCriteria: HTML contains a div with class 'scroll-container' and three nested divs with classes 'item-1', 'item-2', and 'item-3'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have exactly three child divs with the correct class names inside the parent container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTML structure doesn't match what's needed. Check that you have a parent div with class 'scroll-container' and three child divs with classes 'item-1', 'item-2', and 'item-3'.

steps.title: Style the parent container for scrolling
steps.instruction: Add CSS to make the .scroll-container a fixed-size container with scrollable overflow. Set its width to 400px, height to 300px, and overflow to auto.
steps.hint: Use the .scroll-container selector and define width, height, and overflow properties.

<style>
  .scroll-container {
    /* Add width, height, and overflow properties here */
  }
</style>
steps.expectedOutcome: The .scroll-container will have fixed dimensions and become scrollable when content exceeds those dimensions.
successCriteria: The .scroll-container selector has width: 400px, height: 300px, and overflow: auto defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included all three required properties: width, height, and overflow.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container styling isn't complete. Remember to set fixed dimensions and make it scrollable with overflow.

steps.title: Style the child items with distinct colors
steps.instruction: Inside the <style> block, add CSS rules for the .item class to give each child item full container width and height, and assign each item a different background color.
steps.hint: Use width: 100%; and height: 100%; to make each item fill the container. Then set background-color: [color]; for each item with distinct colors like red, blue, green, etc.
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Create your HTML structure here -->

<style>
  .scroll-container {
    /* Add width, height, and overflow properties here */
  }
  
  /* Add CSS for .item here */
</style>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each child item will be styled to fill the scroll container and have distinct background colors for visual differentiation.
successCriteria: CSS rules for .item are added with width: 100%;, height: 100%;, and at least one distinct background-color property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include width: 100%;, height: 100%;, and at least one distinct background-color for the .item class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS for .item is missing or incomplete. Add rules to make items fill the container and give them distinct background colors.

steps.title: Enable scroll-snap on the parent container
steps.instruction: Add the property `scroll-snap-type: y mandatory;` to the `.scroll-container` rule to enable vertical scroll snapping.
steps.hint: Add the property inside the existing `.scroll-container` rule. This tells the browser to snap to child elements when scrolling vertically.
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Create your HTML structure here -->

<style>
  .scroll-container {
    /* Add width, height, and overflow properties here */
    scroll-snap-type: y mandatory;
  }
  
  /* Add CSS for .item here */
</style>
steps.expectedOutcome: The `.scroll-container` rule now includes the `scroll-snap-type` property with `y mandatory` to enable vertical scroll snapping.
successCriteria: The `.scroll-container` rule contains the property `scroll-snap-type: y mandatory;`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added `scroll-snap-type: y mandatory;` exactly as shown inside the `.scroll-container` rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scroll-snap property wasn't added correctly. Check that `scroll-snap-type: y mandatory;` is inside the `.scroll-container` rule.

steps.title: Define scroll-snap alignment on child items
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property scroll-snap-align: start; to the .item selector to make each child item snap to its start edge when scrolling stops.
steps.hint: The scroll-snap-align property controls where an item aligns within the scroll container when snapping occurs. Use 'start' to align to the top edge (for vertical scrolling).
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Create your HTML structure here -->

<style>
  .scroll-container {
    /* Add width, height, and overflow properties here */
    scroll-snap-type: y mandatory;
  }
  
  .item {
    /* Add scroll-snap-align property here */
  }
</style>
steps.expectedOutcome: The .item rule now includes scroll-snap-align: start;, ensuring each item snaps to the top of the container when scrolling stops.
successCriteria: The CSS for .item includes the property scroll-snap-align: start;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the scroll-snap-align property might be missing or have an incorrect value. Make sure you add scroll-snap-align: start; to the .item selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .item selector doesn't have the required scroll-snap-align property. Add scroll-snap-align: start; to control where items snap within the container.

steps.title: Change scroll-snap-type to proximity
steps.instruction: In the .scroll-container rule, change the scroll-snap-type value from 'mandatory' to 'proximity'.
steps.hint: Look for the scroll-snap-type property in your CSS and modify its second value.
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Create your HTML structure here -->

<style>
  .scroll-container {
    /* Add width, height, and overflow properties here */
    scroll-snap-type: y proximity;
  }
  
  .item {
    /* Add scroll-snap-align property here */
  }
</style>
steps.expectedOutcome: The scroll container will now use proximity snapping instead of mandatory snapping.
successCriteria: The .scroll-container rule has scroll-snap-type: y proximity;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you changed 'mandatory' to 'proximity' in the scroll-snap-type property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scroll-snap-type value should be 'proximity' instead of 'mandatory'. Check the .scroll-container rule.

steps.title: Experiment with different scroll-snap-align values
steps.instruction: In the .item CSS rule, change the scroll-snap-align property from 'start' to 'center' on at least one item to see how the alignment behavior changes.
steps.hint: Look for the .item selector in your CSS and modify the scroll-snap-align value there. You can try 'center' or 'end' instead of 'start'.
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Create your HTML structure here -->

<style>
  .scroll-container {
    /* Add width, height, and overflow properties here */
    scroll-snap-type: y proximity;
  }
  
  .item {
    /* Add scroll-snap-align property here */
    scroll-snap-align: start;
  }
</style>
steps.expectedOutcome: The scroll-snap-align property on .item will be updated to 'center' (or 'end'), changing how items align when snapped during scrolling.
successCriteria: The .item CSS rule includes scroll-snap-align: center; (or scroll-snap-align: end;).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've changed the scroll-snap-align property value in the .item rule. Check that it's set to 'center' or 'end'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scroll-snap-align property in the .item rule still shows 'start'. Please update it to 'center' or 'end' to complete this step.

steps.title: Add scroll padding to the container
steps.instruction: Add a scroll-padding property to the .scroll-container rule to create a 20-pixel offset between snapped items and container edges.
steps.hint: Use the scroll-padding property with a value of 20px. This will add space inside the container before the first snapped item and after the last snapped item.
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Create your HTML structure here -->

<style>
  .scroll-container {
    /* Add width, height, and overflow properties here */
    scroll-snap-type: y proximity;
    /* Add scroll-padding property here */
  }
  
  .item {
    /* Add scroll-snap-align property here */
    scroll-snap-align: start;
  }
</style>
steps.expectedOutcome: The .scroll-container rule will include a scroll-padding property that creates visual spacing between the container edges and snapped items during scrolling.
successCriteria: The .scroll-container CSS rule contains a scroll-padding property with the value 20px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the scroll-padding property with the correct value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scroll-padding property is missing or incorrect. Try adding 'scroll-padding: 20px;' to the .scroll-container rule.
